headline: Devils acquire 3-time Vezina winner Connor Hellebuyck from Jets
take:
The Devils have acquired three-time Vezina Trophy winner Connor Hellebuyck from the Jets in a five-player trade, per The Hockey News and ESPN, ending a long standoff between the goalie and Winnipeg. The Athletic calls it a "long, messy saga" and says the deal makes New Jersey a contender.

The numbers show why the Devils wanted him. So far this season, NJD controls 58.6% of expected goals (a measure of shot quality) overall and 60% at five-on-five, yet sits at 6-4-0. The problem is in net: the team's goals saved above expected is -5.3, meaning its goalies have let in about five more goals than the shots should have produced. WPG has the opposite profile. Its goalies sit at +5.6 while the team holds only 46% of expected goals, so the Jets have been leaning on goaltending. Hellebuyck's departure leaves that propped-up record exposed.

For New Jersey, a goalie of his caliber could turn strong process into wins. Dawson Mercer is a case in point. He has no goals and four points in 10 games despite 2.18 expected goals of his own, a gap of -2.18. Better goaltending would help the whole team convert its edge, but Mercer's finishing is a separate fix.
